Repolarisation is prolonged with a long isoelectric ST segment and a late broad T wave: QT ~515 ms, Bazett QTc ~522 ms. The prior tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07) showed atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response (mean 47 bpm, RMSSD 189 ms) and QTc 419 ms. Amiodarone was started 2025-11-10, so sinus rhythm has been restored (resolved atrial fibrillation) at the cost of a QTc rise of more than 60 ms to above 500 ms.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 111 bpm (RR coefficient of variation 0.01) with a small P wave identifiable before each QRS at PR ~128 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +60 deg, QTc ~409 ms. The prior day's tracing (106143775, 2025-03-07) was also a regular sinus tachycardia at 116 bpm with QTc 351 ms; the 58 ms QTc rise is below the 60 ms threshold, and there is no rhythm or conduction change.

Atrial fibrillation: markedly irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.28, RMSSD 249 ms) at a mean ventricular rate of about 99 bpm with no discernible P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -59 deg (left axis deviation, qR in I/aVL with deep S in II/III/aVF - left anterior fascicular block pattern). QTc ~421 ms. Only ECG available for this patient, so no prior comparison. Confirms the documented atrial fibrillation for which warfarin is prescribed.

Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, PR 136 ms, QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +42 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~444 ms. The prior tracing (100698634, 2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with PR 128 ms and QTc ~420 ms; rate has slowed but there is no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with a P wave before every QRS (PR 120 ms). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +39 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~457 ms (borderline prolonged but below the 500 ms review threshold). Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.33-0.55 s, RMSSD 98 ms) at a mean rate of about 144 bpm, with a fibrillatory baseline and no organised P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +7 deg, QTc ~357 ms. The tracing two hours earlier the same day (107914094, 17:13) showed the same rhythm at 139 bpm with QTc 368 ms - no change. This directly contradicts the same-day clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' (flagged as a documentation conflict).

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, PR 154 ms, QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -28 deg (borderline leftward but within the normal range); lead II is nearly isoelectric. QTc (Bazett) ~443 ms. The prior tracing (104232242, 2025-04-27) was sinus at 60 bpm with QTc 405 ms; no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with a P wave before every QRS (PR 116 ms). QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +6 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~425 ms (the T wave has a slow terminal limb, so the estimate carries roughly +/-30 ms uncertainty). Only ECG for this patient, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregular RR intervals (RMSSD 66 ms, 48% of successive intervals differing by >50 ms) at a mean of about 144 bpm, no organised P waves and therefore no measurable PR interval. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis -5 deg, QTc ~356 ms. The tracing four days earlier (102456968, 2024-06-25) was regular sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with PR 154 ms and a long QTc of ~487 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new and QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms (partly rate related).

Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with an upright, consistent P wave before every QRS (PR 184 ms). QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +53 deg. QTc (Bazett) ~378 ms - normal, which is relevant because citalopram 40 mg daily had been started five days earlier. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible. Consistent with the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +24 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~419 ms - normal repolarisation. Only ECG in the chart; it predates the 2026-08-01 start of escitalopram, so it does not satisfy the required post-initiation ECG.

Irregularly irregular rhythm with a slow mean ventricular rate of about 53 bpm (RR 0.69-1.16 s, RMSSD 288 ms) and no organised P waves on any lead - atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response; no measurable PR interval. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +32 deg, QTc ~446 ms. The tracing three days earlier (107873952, 2024-11-12) was regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a clear P wave (PR 176 ms) and QTc 401 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new. Nursing documentation that day recorded mixed rhythms including junctional rhythm and atrial fibrillation.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.18, RMSSD 107 ms) at a mean of about 139 bpm, no P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis -9 deg, QTc ~365 ms. The prior tracing (108184246, 2024-08-18) was also atrial fibrillation at 132 bpm with QTc 374 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with occasional ectopy, PR 170 ms, QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -81 deg: marked left axis deviation (qR in I and aVL, rS in II, III and aVF) consistent with left anterior fascicular block. QTc (Bazett) ~371 ms. The prior tracing (102857516, 2024-02-01) was sinus at 78 bpm, PR 190 ms, axis -66 deg, QTc 392 ms - no significant change.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia, PR 112 ms, QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +66 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~412 ms. The prior day's tracing (106045460, 2025-03-08) was essentially identical (sinus 62 bpm, PR 112 ms, QTc 432 ms); no change. This baseline predates the 2026-09-15 start of haloperidol, so a repeat ECG is still required.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, very regular, PR 152 ms, QRS 66 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +58 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~401 ms. Entirely normal tracing. Only ECG available, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation: grossly irregular RR intervals (0.44-1.55 s, coefficient of variation 0.24, RMSSD 367 ms) at a mean ventricular rate of about 70 bpm with a fibrillatory baseline and no organised P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 68 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +135 deg (right axis deviation - lead I net negative, aVF positive). QTc ~409 ms. Only ECG for this patient; nursing documentation the same day also records atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular, PR 158 ms, QRS 68 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +67 deg. QTc (Bazett) is borderline prolonged at about 490 ms (noisy baseline, estimate +/-40 ms). The prior tracing (109048192, 2020-02-02) was also sinus rhythm at 75 bpm (a single artefactual short interval aside) with QTc ~531 ms; no rhythm or conduction change and the QTc difference is under 60 ms.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.17, RMSSD 99 ms) at a mean of about 134 bpm, no organised P waves, no measurable PR interval. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +52 deg, QTc ~379 ms. The prior tracing (108234665, 2024-09-28) was sinus rhythm at 59 bpm with PR 156 ms and QTc ~378 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; QTc unchanged. Nursing documentation on 2025-07-08 also records atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 78 bpm, PR ~150 ms, QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +47 deg. T waves are of very low amplitude and bifid, giving an uncertain QTc of roughly 470 ms (+/-40 ms). The prior day's tracing (108530691, 2025-10-17) was sinus at 85 bpm with equally flat T waves and QTc ~415 ms; rhythm and conduction unchanged and the QTc difference does not reliably reach 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm, PR 162 ms, QRS 94 ms (no bundle branch block), frontal axis +8 deg, QTc ~400 ms. Compared with the tracing two days earlier (102573205, 2026-02-17: sinus 83 bpm, PR 146 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 398 ms) there is no significant change - same rhythm, no new conduction abnormality and QTc within 2 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm. The P wave begins about 210 ms before the QRS, i.e. first-degree AV block (PR >200 ms). QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +3 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~377 ms. The prior tracing (103042067, 2024-11-30) was sinus at 51 bpm with PR 184 ms and QTc 358 ms, so PR has lengthened slightly; rhythm unchanged, no new bundle branch block and QTc change well under 60 ms.

Paced rhythm at 112 bpm. Two narrow, high-amplitude pacing spikes (slew several times greater than the QRS itself) precede each complex, about 110 ms and 80 ms before the R peak, followed by a wide 152 ms paced QRS with a markedly rightward frontal axis (about +131 deg; dominant negativity in I/aVL and tall R in III/aVF). No intrinsic P wave is visible, so no PR interval can be measured, and the intraventricular conduction pattern cannot be classified as right or left bundle branch block in a paced complex. QTc ~412 ms. The prior tracing (103417522, 2020-11-03) had no pacing spikes: a regular rhythm at 109 bpm with a very wide 192 ms QRS of left bundle branch block morphology (QS in V1-V2, broad monophasic R in V6) and QTc ~448 ms. Pacing is therefore new.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.19, RMSSD 104 ms) at a mean of about 152 bpm, no organised atrial activity and no measurable PR interval. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis -10 deg, QTc ~354 ms. The previous day's tracing (107374881, 2025-09-12) was sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with a clear P wave (PR 150 ms) and QTc 412 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; the QTc fall of 58 ms is just below the reporting threshold and is largely rate related. Nursing documentation on 2025-09-13 records both sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.20, RMSSD 127 ms) at a mean of about 152 bpm with no organised P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +73 deg, QTc ~346 ms. The prior tracing (107132278, 2025-01-06) was regular sinus rhythm at 86 bpm with PR 126 ms and QTc ~450 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new and the Bazett QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms (mostly an artefact of the much faster rate).

Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 72 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +33 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~412 ms. The prior tracing (109840765, 2021-04-20) was sinus at 81 bpm with PR 166 ms and QTc 392 ms; no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with a prominent P wave before each QRS (PR 170 ms). QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +14 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~394 ms. The tracing two days earlier (105362569, 2025-11-21) was also sinus rhythm (67 bpm, PR 158 ms) but with a QTc of about 527 ms, so QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms and has normalised. This tracing matches the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, regular, PR 174 ms, QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +23 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~424 ms. The prior tracing (100851619, 2026-02-24) was sinus at 70 bpm with PR 160 ms, a slightly wider 112 ms QRS (non-specific intraventricular conduction delay, not meeting bundle branch block criteria) and QTc 438 ms; no qualifying change.

Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.14, RMSSD 161 ms) at a mean ventricular rate of about 63 bpm with no organised P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 102 ms - mild non-specific intraventricular conduction delay, not meeting criteria for right or left bundle branch block. Frontal axis +65 deg. T waves are low amplitude; QTc ~400 ms (+/-40 ms). The prior tracing (101950824, 2026-01-01) was also atrial fibrillation (mean 102 bpm, QRS 104 ms, QTc ~411 ms): no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Nursing documentation on 2026-01-21 also records atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm with a well-formed P wave before each QRS (PR 186 ms, upper normal but not first-degree AV block). QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +62 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~419 ms. Only ECG for this patient, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, very regular, with a P wave (positive in II, negative terminal component in V1) before each QRS at PR 166 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +38 deg, QTc ~404 ms. No atrial flutter is present on this tracing despite the documented flutter diagnosis. The prior tracing (102955795, 2022-07-04) was also sinus tachycardia at 115 bpm with PR 174 ms and QTc 395 ms; no change.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm with a discrete P wave preceding each QRS (PR 192 ms, upper normal). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +51 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~391 ms. The prior tracing (106186980, 2016-09-16) was also sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm with PR 176 ms and QTc 402 ms; no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm. The underlying RR intervals are regular at about 0.97 s with one premature beat (0.54 s) followed by a compensatory pause (1.37 s), and a consistent P wave precedes each sinus beat at PR ~200 ms - this is sinus rhythm with an isolated premature complex, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -34 deg (left axis deviation). QTc (Bazett) ~434 ms (low-amplitude T waves, +/-40 ms). Only ECG for this patient. Note that paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented in the chart and is not captured on this single tracing.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm with a small consistent atrial deflection about 140 ms before each QRS - sinus rhythm (nursing documentation the same day records normal sinus rhythm). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block. The frontal axis is about -171 deg, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant: lead I and lead II are both deeply negative while aVR is positive, a pattern that in practice usually reflects left/right arm lead reversal and should prompt a repeat tracing with checked electrode placement. QTc (Bazett) ~378 ms. Only ECG for this patient.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 122 ms, QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +44 deg. Repolarisation is clearly prolonged: QT ~490 ms with a Bazett QTc of about 530 ms. The prior tracing (107149156, 2020-06-17) was sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QTc ~374 ms, so QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. The patient remains on citalopram 40 mg daily (flagged separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +68 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~445 ms - below the 500 ms review threshold. Only ECG for this patient. This tracing was obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started and satisfies the post-initiation ECG requirement.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, PR 174 ms, QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis -9 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~357 ms. The prior tracing (108651109, 2018-12-13) was sinus at 66 bpm with a longer PR of 204 ms; nursing documentation that day noted intermittent atrial pacing. No rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change (391 -> 357 ms).

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm - RR intervals are 0.40-0.45 s with a coefficient of variation of only 0.02 and RMSSD 11 ms, i.e. regular, excluding atrial fibrillation - with low-amplitude atrial activity preceding each QRS (PR ~178 ms) and no sawtooth flutter waves on spectral analysis of the QRST-subtracted signal; this is best classified as sinus tachycardia. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +5 deg, QTc ~362 ms. The prior tracing (109839112, 2022-07-11) was atrial fibrillation (mean 110 bpm, coefficient of variation 0.24, RMSSD 190 ms, no P waves), so atrial fibrillation has resolved. Nursing notes on 2022-07-13 still record atrial fibrillation and atrial pacing, so the classification of this single tracing should be confirmed clinically.
Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 98 ms (upper normal, no bundle branch block), frontal axis +35 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~450 ms. Only ECG for this patient, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response: grossly irregular RR intervals (0.63-1.86 s, coefficient of variation 0.25, RMSSD 436 ms) at a mean of about 53 bpm, with no organised P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 106 ms - non-specific intraventricular conduction delay that does not meet criteria for right or left bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -33 deg (borderline left axis deviation). QTc ~412 ms. The prior tracing (100466541, 2024-09-04) was also atrial fibrillation (mean 81 bpm, QRS 108 ms, QTc 407 ms): no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular RR, coefficient of variation 0.21, RMSSD 172 ms, no organised P waves, no measurable PR interval) at a mean ventricular rate of about 99 bpm, with a very wide 158 ms QRS showing a QS complex in V1-V2 and a broad monophasic R in V5-V6 and lead I - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -16 deg. QTc ~429 ms. The tracing four days earlier (103262474, 2024-12-03) was regular sinus rhythm at 79 bpm with first-degree AV block (PR 240 ms) and a 146 ms QRS of right bundle branch block morphology (terminal broad R in V1 with wide S waves in I and V6) and marked left axis deviation. Therefore atrial fibrillation is new, the previous right bundle branch block has resolved and a new left bundle branch block has appeared; QTc change (474 -> 429 ms) is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 126 ms, QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +51 deg. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: QT ~485 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 518 ms. Compared with the prior ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23: sinus 75 bpm, QTc 361 ms) QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. This is the most recent tracing and the patient remains on escitalopram, so the prolongation is clinically actionable (flagged separately as a QT safety item).

Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (RMSSD 251 ms, 92% of successive intervals differing by >50 ms) at a mean ventricular rate of about 87 bpm, with no organised atrial activity, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +50 deg, QTc ~450 ms. The previous day's tracing (109550629, 2024-10-30) was also atrial fibrillation (mean 65 bpm, QTc 436 ms): no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with a P wave before each QRS at PR 140 ms. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +69 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~406 ms. This is the only ECG for this patient, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 101 bpm with PR 150 ms, QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +62 deg and QTc ~421 ms. The immediately preceding tracing from the same day (102910502, 2021-08-23) is essentially identical (sinus 101 bpm, PR 154 ms, QTc 419 ms); no change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, with a low-amplitude but consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 170 ms). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +41 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~403 ms. The prior tracing (104629882, 2023-05-22) was also sinus at 57 bpm with a single premature beat and QTc 395 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Notably no atrial fibrillation is captured on either tracing although the patient carries that diagnosis and takes warfarin.

items.explanation: Two current oral anticoagulant orders overlap: apixaban 5 mg BID (authored 2026-07-15, valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (authored 2026-07-15, valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was re-prescribed the same day and was never stopped, so both remain active as of 2026-09-24. Concurrent DOAC therapy markedly increases bleeding risk and requires immediate reconciliation.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (order authored that day, note aa0ab6aa). The start date falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-03-01, so the original 2025-09-01 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (The QTc on that tracing is 522 ms and is flagged separately under QT_SAFETY.)

Citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (order authored 2026-03-02, note 55f064b7). Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised 2026-03-01 memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met; that tracing shows sinus rhythm with QTc 378 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (order authored 2026-02-12, note f10bacd5). The start predates 2026-03-01, so the earlier 30-day window of the 2025-09-01 memo applies and an ECG was required by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met; QTc on that tracing is 445 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (order authored 2026-04-10, note 93604d42). Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo applies: an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was not recorded until 2026-04-29 - 19 days after the start and 5 days past the deadline - so the requirement was not met within the required time and remains unsatisfied as of 2026-09-24. (That late tracing showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with QTc 378 ms, and escitalopram remains current through 2027-01-03.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (order authored 2026-08-01, note fa831ef2). Start on/after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722) and none appears after the start date, so the required post-initiation ECG is overdue as of 2026-08-15.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (order authored 2026-08-10, note a8e85155). Start on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists for this patient in the clinic record, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (5e12a8aa) states the patient reports an ECG performed at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - with the report requested by fax and not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily, a QT watch-list medication, was newly started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (order authored 2026-09-15, note 33136968; no prior haloperidol in the chart). Start on/after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09 (104253928, QTc 412 ms), but as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation the deadline has not yet passed, so the requirement is pending rather than overdue.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 2026-09-01 by Dr. Paul Kessler records "INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR" - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician after 2026-03-01, so the 2026-03-01 memo requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was drawn on 2026-09-05, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

The anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD records "Home INR 3.4. Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol" - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist under the standing order, after 2026-03-01, so an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change; no INR has been drawn since. The follow-up INR is overdue as of 2026-09-17 in a 95-year-old on amiodarone (which potentiates warfarin) with CKD stage 3.

71-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 42731; carried in the history of every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease from coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). No anticoagulant has ever been prescribed - the only current outpatient order is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily (valid 2026-07-28 to 2027-01-01). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation (score >=2 in a man) is absent; note prior hemorrhage complicating a procedure should be weighed when selecting therapy.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0) and prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis (I63.40, I63.9, I69.354). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2, female 1). Current outpatient medications are only metoprolol tartrate, carvedilol and famotidine (all valid through late 2026/2027); no anticoagulant is ordered and none appears anywhere in the record. Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention. Thrombocytopenia, non-ruptured cerebral aneurysm and a history of falling are documented and should be weighed in the risk/benefit discussion, but none is recorded as a decision to withhold therapy.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 2026-08-20 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nonetheless re-ordered (valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) and remains current on 2026-09-24, together with aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg daily - triple antithrombotic therapy after a recent major GI bleed. The required cardiology review of whether to resume anticoagulation is not documented.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72." Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Nursing rhythm documentation on 2026-06-10 also records atrial fibrillation. The charted rhythm and rate contradict the tracings and the patient (unspecified atrial fibrillation, on warfarin) needs rate/rhythm reassessment.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug per the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo) is current (order 2026-04-23, valid to 2027-01-02) and has been continued without interruption since 2024-05-14. The patient's most recent 12-lead ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT approximately 485 ms and Bazett QTc approximately 518 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which the clinic document requires the prescriber to review. Notably the 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this same tracing as "QT acceptable"; QTc had risen from 361 ms on the prior ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23). Most recent electrolytes are normal (K 4.1 mEq/L and Mg 2.1 mg/dL, both 2025-08-23). No ECG has been obtained since 2023.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) is current (order 2026-07-29, valid to 2027-01-05) and has been continuous since it was started on 2025-11-10 for atrial fibrillation. The most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with a markedly prolonged repolarisation: QT approximately 515 ms, Bazett QTc approximately 522 ms (>=500 ms), up from 419 ms on the pre-amiodarone tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07). Prescriber review is required by the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo. Most recent electrolytes (2026-04-20) are normal: K 4.4 mEq/L, Mg 2.2 mg/dL. Also on warfarin, which amiodarone potentiates.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) is current (order 2026-05-29, valid to 2026-12-25) and has been continuous since 2023-10-02; 40 mg also exceeds the usual maximum recommended for QT reasons. The most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT approximately 490 ms and Bazett QTc approximately 530 ms (>=500 ms), compared with 374 ms on the prior tracing (107149156, 2020-06-17). Prescriber review is required by the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. Documented syncope and type 1 diabetes add to the concern; no ECG has been obtained since 2023.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) is current (order 2026-08-22, valid to 2027-01-05) and has been continuous since 2022-03-01. The most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT approximately 545 ms and Bazett QTc approximately 533 ms (>=500 ms); the pre-conversion tracing three weeks earlier (100867733, 2022-04-06) was atrial fibrillation with QTc 375 ms, so QTc rose by well over 60 ms after amiodarone was started. Prescriber review is required by the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14) K 4.1 mEq/L and Mg 1.8 mg/dL (low-normal magnesium). Additional risk: age 95, CKD stage 3, and concomitant warfarin/metoprolol. No ECG since 2022.

interpretations.explanation: Irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 131 bpm (RR 0.36-0.62 s, RMSSD 143 ms) with no organised P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis +57 deg, no bundle branch block. QTc (Bazett) ~354 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (107819285, 11:18) was regular sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with clear P waves (PR 122 ms), so atrial fibrillation is new; QTc essentially unchanged (390 -> 354 ms).

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular, with a P wave before each QRS (PR ~150 ms). QRS is now narrow at 82 ms; the frontal axis is rightward (net negative lead I, positive aVF, about +135 deg). QTc ~387 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (106516875, 2024-12-05) showed a 144 ms QRS with an rSR' pattern and a broad terminal R in V1 plus wide S waves in I/V6 - right bundle branch block - which has resolved on this tracing; QTc also fell from 470 to 387 ms (>60 ms decrease). Most likely a transient rate-related right bundle branch block.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with a small but consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 174 ms). QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +69 deg. Repolarisation is prolonged with a long isoelectric ST segment and a late broad T wave: QT ~515 ms, Bazett QTc ~522 ms. The prior tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07) showed atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response (mean 47 bpm, RMSSD 189 ms) and QTc 419 ms. Amiodarone was started 2025-11-10, so sinus rhythm has been restored (resolved atrial fibrillation) at the cost of a QTc rise of more than 60 ms to above 500 ms.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 111 bpm (RR coefficient of variation 0.01) with a small P wave identifiable before each QRS at PR ~128 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +60 deg, QTc ~409 ms. The prior day's tracing (106143775, 2025-03-07) was also a regular sinus tachycardia at 116 bpm with QTc 351 ms; the 58 ms QTc rise is below the 60 ms threshold, and there is no rhythm or conduction change.

Atrial fibrillation: markedly irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.28, RMSSD 249 ms) at a mean ventricular rate of about 99 bpm with no discernible P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -59 deg (left axis deviation, qR in I/aVL with deep S in II/III/aVF - left anterior fascicular block pattern). QTc ~421 ms. Only ECG available for this patient, so no prior comparison. Confirms the documented atrial fibrillation for which warfarin is prescribed.

Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, PR 136 ms, QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +42 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~444 ms. The prior tracing (100698634, 2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with PR 128 ms and QTc ~420 ms; rate has slowed but there is no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with a P wave before every QRS (PR 120 ms). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +39 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~457 ms (borderline prolonged but below the 500 ms review threshold). Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.33-0.55 s, RMSSD 98 ms) at a mean rate of about 144 bpm, with a fibrillatory baseline and no organised P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +7 deg, QTc ~357 ms. The tracing two hours earlier the same day (107914094, 17:13) showed the same rhythm at 139 bpm with QTc 368 ms - no change. This directly contradicts the same-day clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' (flagged as a documentation conflict).

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, PR 154 ms, QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -28 deg (borderline leftward but within the normal range); lead II is nearly isoelectric. QTc (Bazett) ~443 ms. The prior tracing (104232242, 2025-04-27) was sinus at 60 bpm with QTc 405 ms; no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with a P wave before every QRS (PR 116 ms). QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +6 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~425 ms (the T wave has a slow terminal limb, so the estimate carries roughly +/-30 ms uncertainty). Only ECG for this patient, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregular RR intervals (RMSSD 66 ms, 48% of successive intervals differing by >50 ms) at a mean of about 144 bpm, no organised P waves and therefore no measurable PR interval. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis -5 deg, QTc ~356 ms. The tracing four days earlier (102456968, 2024-06-25) was regular sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with PR 154 ms and a long QTc of ~487 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new and QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms (partly rate related).

Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with an upright, consistent P wave before every QRS (PR 184 ms). QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +53 deg. QTc (Bazett) ~378 ms - normal, which is relevant because citalopram 40 mg daily had been started five days earlier. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible. Consistent with the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +24 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~419 ms - normal repolarisation. Only ECG in the chart; it predates the 2026-08-01 start of escitalopram, so it does not satisfy the required post-initiation ECG.

Irregularly irregular rhythm with a slow mean ventricular rate of about 53 bpm (RR 0.69-1.16 s, RMSSD 288 ms) and no organised P waves on any lead - atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response; no measurable PR interval. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +32 deg, QTc ~446 ms. The tracing three days earlier (107873952, 2024-11-12) was regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a clear P wave (PR 176 ms) and QTc 401 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new. Nursing documentation that day recorded mixed rhythms including junctional rhythm and atrial fibrillation.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.18, RMSSD 107 ms) at a mean of about 139 bpm, no P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis -9 deg, QTc ~365 ms. The prior tracing (108184246, 2024-08-18) was also atrial fibrillation at 132 bpm with QTc 374 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with occasional ectopy, PR 170 ms, QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -81 deg: marked left axis deviation (qR in I and aVL, rS in II, III and aVF) consistent with left anterior fascicular block. QTc (Bazett) ~371 ms. The prior tracing (102857516, 2024-02-01) was sinus at 78 bpm, PR 190 ms, axis -66 deg, QTc 392 ms - no significant change.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia, PR 112 ms, QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +66 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~412 ms. The prior day's tracing (106045460, 2025-03-08) was essentially identical (sinus 62 bpm, PR 112 ms, QTc 432 ms); no change. This baseline predates the 2026-09-15 start of haloperidol, so a repeat ECG is still required.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, very regular, PR 152 ms, QRS 66 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +58 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~401 ms. Entirely normal tracing. Only ECG available, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation: grossly irregular RR intervals (0.44-1.55 s, coefficient of variation 0.24, RMSSD 367 ms) at a mean ventricular rate of about 70 bpm with a fibrillatory baseline and no organised P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 68 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +135 deg (right axis deviation - lead I net negative, aVF positive). QTc ~409 ms. Only ECG for this patient; nursing documentation the same day also records atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular, PR 158 ms, QRS 68 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +67 deg. QTc (Bazett) is borderline prolonged at about 490 ms (noisy baseline, estimate +/-40 ms). The prior tracing (109048192, 2020-02-02) was also sinus rhythm at 75 bpm (a single artefactual short interval aside) with QTc ~531 ms; no rhythm or conduction change and the QTc difference is under 60 ms.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.17, RMSSD 99 ms) at a mean of about 134 bpm, no organised P waves, no measurable PR interval. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +52 deg, QTc ~379 ms. The prior tracing (108234665, 2024-09-28) was sinus rhythm at 59 bpm with PR 156 ms and QTc ~378 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; QTc unchanged. Nursing documentation on 2025-07-08 also records atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 78 bpm, PR ~150 ms, QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +47 deg. T waves are of very low amplitude and bifid, giving an uncertain QTc of roughly 470 ms (+/-40 ms). The prior day's tracing (108530691, 2025-10-17) was sinus at 85 bpm with equally flat T waves and QTc ~415 ms; rhythm and conduction unchanged and the QTc difference does not reliably reach 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm, PR 162 ms, QRS 94 ms (no bundle branch block), frontal axis +8 deg, QTc ~400 ms. Compared with the tracing two days earlier (102573205, 2026-02-17: sinus 83 bpm, PR 146 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 398 ms) there is no significant change - same rhythm, no new conduction abnormality and QTc within 2 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm. The P wave begins about 210 ms before the QRS, i.e. first-degree AV block (PR >200 ms). QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +3 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~377 ms. The prior tracing (103042067, 2024-11-30) was sinus at 51 bpm with PR 184 ms and QTc 358 ms, so PR has lengthened slightly; rhythm unchanged, no new bundle branch block and QTc change well under 60 ms.

Paced rhythm at 112 bpm. Two narrow, high-amplitude pacing spikes (slew several times greater than the QRS itself) precede each complex, about 110 ms and 80 ms before the R peak, followed by a wide 152 ms paced QRS with a markedly rightward frontal axis (about +131 deg; dominant negativity in I/aVL and tall R in III/aVF). No intrinsic P wave is visible, so no PR interval can be measured, and the intraventricular conduction pattern cannot be classified as right or left bundle branch block in a paced complex. QTc ~412 ms. The prior tracing (103417522, 2020-11-03) had no pacing spikes: a regular rhythm at 109 bpm with a very wide 192 ms QRS of left bundle branch block morphology (QS in V1-V2, broad monophasic R in V6) and QTc ~448 ms. Pacing is therefore new.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.19, RMSSD 104 ms) at a mean of about 152 bpm, no organised atrial activity and no measurable PR interval. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis -10 deg, QTc ~354 ms. The previous day's tracing (107374881, 2025-09-12) was sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with a clear P wave (PR 150 ms) and QTc 412 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; the QTc fall of 58 ms is just below the reporting threshold and is largely rate related. Nursing documentation on 2025-09-13 records both sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.20, RMSSD 127 ms) at a mean of about 152 bpm with no organised P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +73 deg, QTc ~346 ms. The prior tracing (107132278, 2025-01-06) was regular sinus rhythm at 86 bpm with PR 126 ms and QTc ~450 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new and the Bazett QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms (mostly an artefact of the much faster rate).

Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 72 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +33 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~412 ms. The prior tracing (109840765, 2021-04-20) was sinus at 81 bpm with PR 166 ms and QTc 392 ms; no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with a prominent P wave before each QRS (PR 170 ms). QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +14 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~394 ms. The tracing two days earlier (105362569, 2025-11-21) was also sinus rhythm (67 bpm, PR 158 ms) but with a QTc of about 527 ms, so QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms and has normalised. This tracing matches the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, regular, PR 174 ms, QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +23 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~424 ms. The prior tracing (100851619, 2026-02-24) was sinus at 70 bpm with PR 160 ms, a slightly wider 112 ms QRS (non-specific intraventricular conduction delay, not meeting bundle branch block criteria) and QTc 438 ms; no qualifying change.

Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.14, RMSSD 161 ms) at a mean ventricular rate of about 63 bpm with no organised P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 102 ms - mild non-specific intraventricular conduction delay, not meeting criteria for right or left bundle branch block. Frontal axis +65 deg. T waves are low amplitude; QTc ~400 ms (+/-40 ms). The prior tracing (101950824, 2026-01-01) was also atrial fibrillation (mean 102 bpm, QRS 104 ms, QTc ~411 ms): no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Nursing documentation on 2026-01-21 also records atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm with a well-formed P wave before each QRS (PR 186 ms, upper normal but not first-degree AV block). QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +62 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~419 ms. Only ECG for this patient, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, very regular, with a P wave (positive in II, negative terminal component in V1) before each QRS at PR 166 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +38 deg, QTc ~404 ms. No atrial flutter is present on this tracing despite the documented flutter diagnosis. The prior tracing (102955795, 2022-07-04) was also sinus tachycardia at 115 bpm with PR 174 ms and QTc 395 ms; no change.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm with a discrete P wave preceding each QRS (PR 192 ms, upper normal). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +51 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~391 ms. The prior tracing (106186980, 2016-09-16) was also sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm with PR 176 ms and QTc 402 ms; no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm. The underlying RR intervals are regular at about 0.97 s with one premature beat (0.54 s) followed by a compensatory pause (1.37 s), and a consistent P wave precedes each sinus beat at PR ~200 ms - this is sinus rhythm with an isolated premature complex, not atrial fibrillation. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -34 deg (left axis deviation). QTc (Bazett) ~434 ms (low-amplitude T waves, +/-40 ms). Only ECG for this patient. Note that paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented in the chart and is not captured on this single tracing.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm with a small consistent atrial deflection about 140 ms before each QRS - sinus rhythm (nursing documentation the same day records normal sinus rhythm). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block. The frontal axis is about -171 deg, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant: lead I and lead II are both deeply negative while aVR is positive, a pattern that in practice usually reflects left/right arm lead reversal and should prompt a repeat tracing with checked electrode placement. QTc (Bazett) ~378 ms. Only ECG for this patient.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 122 ms, QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +44 deg. Repolarisation is clearly prolonged: QT ~490 ms with a Bazett QTc of about 530 ms. The prior tracing (107149156, 2020-06-17) was sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QTc ~374 ms, so QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. The patient remains on citalopram 40 mg daily (flagged separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +68 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~445 ms - below the 500 ms review threshold. Only ECG for this patient. This tracing was obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started and satisfies the post-initiation ECG requirement.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, PR 174 ms, QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis -9 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~357 ms. The prior tracing (108651109, 2018-12-13) was sinus at 66 bpm with a longer PR of 204 ms; nursing documentation that day noted intermittent atrial pacing. No rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change (391 -> 357 ms).

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm - RR intervals are 0.40-0.45 s with a coefficient of variation of only 0.02 and RMSSD 11 ms, i.e. regular, excluding atrial fibrillation - with low-amplitude atrial activity preceding each QRS (PR ~178 ms) and no sawtooth flutter waves on spectral analysis of the QRST-subtracted signal; this is best classified as sinus tachycardia. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +5 deg, QTc ~362 ms. The prior tracing (109839112, 2022-07-11) was atrial fibrillation (mean 110 bpm, coefficient of variation 0.24, RMSSD 190 ms, no P waves), so atrial fibrillation has resolved. Nursing notes on 2022-07-13 still record atrial fibrillation and atrial pacing, so the classification of this single tracing should be confirmed clinically.
Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 98 ms (upper normal, no bundle branch block), frontal axis +35 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~450 ms. Only ECG for this patient, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response: grossly irregular RR intervals (0.63-1.86 s, coefficient of variation 0.25, RMSSD 436 ms) at a mean of about 53 bpm, with no organised P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 106 ms - non-specific intraventricular conduction delay that does not meet criteria for right or left bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -33 deg (borderline left axis deviation). QTc ~412 ms. The prior tracing (100466541, 2024-09-04) was also atrial fibrillation (mean 81 bpm, QRS 108 ms, QTc 407 ms): no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular RR, coefficient of variation 0.21, RMSSD 172 ms, no organised P waves, no measurable PR interval) at a mean ventricular rate of about 99 bpm, with a very wide 158 ms QRS showing a QS complex in V1-V2 and a broad monophasic R in V5-V6 and lead I - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -16 deg. QTc ~429 ms. The tracing four days earlier (103262474, 2024-12-03) was regular sinus rhythm at 79 bpm with first-degree AV block (PR 240 ms) and a 146 ms QRS of right bundle branch block morphology (terminal broad R in V1 with wide S waves in I and V6) and marked left axis deviation. Therefore atrial fibrillation is new, the previous right bundle branch block has resolved and a new left bundle branch block has appeared; QTc change (474 -> 429 ms) is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular, PR 128 ms, QRS 78 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis -24 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~419 ms. The prior tracing (102616671, 2021-05-16) was sinus at 87 bpm with PR 142 ms and QTc 393 ms; no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 126 ms, QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +51 deg. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: QT ~485 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 518 ms. Compared with the prior ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23: sinus 75 bpm, QTc 361 ms) QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. This is the most recent tracing and the patient remains on escitalopram, so the prolongation is clinically actionable (flagged separately as a QT safety item).

Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (RMSSD 251 ms, 92% of successive intervals differing by >50 ms) at a mean ventricular rate of about 87 bpm, with no organised atrial activity, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +50 deg, QTc ~450 ms. The previous day's tracing (109550629, 2024-10-30) was also atrial fibrillation (mean 65 bpm, QTc 436 ms): no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with a P wave before each QRS at PR 140 ms. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +69 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~406 ms. This is the only ECG for this patient, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 101 bpm with PR 150 ms, QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +62 deg and QTc ~421 ms. The immediately preceding tracing from the same day (102910502, 2021-08-23) is essentially identical (sinus 101 bpm, PR 154 ms, QTc 419 ms); no change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, with a low-amplitude but consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 170 ms). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +41 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~403 ms. The prior tracing (104629882, 2023-05-22) was also sinus at 57 bpm with a single premature beat and QTc 395 ms - no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Notably no atrial fibrillation is captured on either tracing although the patient carries that diagnosis and takes warfarin.

arguments.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with first-degree AV block (PR 218 ms). QRS is widened to 126 ms with a deep QS pattern in V1-V2, a broad notched monophasic R in V6 and lead I and no septal q waves - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -24 deg. QTc (Bazett) ~476 ms (partly secondary to the conduction delay). The prior tracing (103686933, 2024-06-03) was essentially the same: sinus 68 bpm, PR 220 ms, QRS 124 ms with the same left bundle branch block, QTc ~465 ms. No new rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

items.explanation: Two current oral anticoagulant orders overlap: apixaban 5 mg BID (authored 2026-07-15, valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (authored 2026-07-15, valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was re-prescribed the same day and was never stopped, so both remain active as of 2026-09-24. Concurrent DOAC therapy markedly increases bleeding risk and requires immediate reconciliation.

The start date falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-03-01, so the original 2025-09-01 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (The QTc on that tracing is 522 ms and is flagged separately under QT_SAFETY.)

Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised 2026-03-01 memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met; that tracing shows sinus rhythm with QTc 378 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (order authored 2026-02-12, note f10bacd5). ECG 101538691 was recorded on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met; QTc on that tracing is 445 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (order authored 2026-04-10, note 93604d42). Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo applies: an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was not recorded until 2026-04-29 - 19 days after the start and 5 days past the deadline - so the requirement was not met within the required time and remains unsatisfied as of 2026-09-24. (That late tracing showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with QTc 378 ms, and escitalopram remains current through 2027-01-03.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (order authored 2026-08-01, note fa831ef2). Start on/after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722) and none appears after the start date, so the required post-initiation ECG is overdue as of 2026-08-15.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (order authored 2026-08-10, note a8e85155). Start on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists for this patient in the clinic record, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (5e12a8aa) states the patient reports an ECG performed at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - with the report requested by fax and not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily, a QT watch-list medication, was newly started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (order authored 2026-09-15, note 33136968; no prior haloperidol in the chart). Start on/after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09 (104253928, QTc 412 ms), but as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation the deadline has not yet passed, so the requirement is pending rather than overdue.

The Cardiology Clinic note of 2026-09-01 by Dr. Paul Kessler records "INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR" - a warfarin dose change made by a clinic clinician after 2026-03-01, so the 2026-03-01 memo requires an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was drawn on 2026-09-05, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol" - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist under the standing order, after 2026-03-01, so an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change; no INR has been drawn since. The follow-up INR is overdue as of 2026-09-17 in a 95-year-old on amiodarone (which potentiates warfarin) with CKD stage 3.

71-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 42731; carried in the history of every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease from coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). No anticoagulant has ever been prescribed - the only current outpatient order is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily (valid 2026-07-28 to 2027-01-01). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation (score >=2 in a man) is absent; note prior hemorrhage complicating a procedure should be weighed when selecting therapy.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0) and prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis (I63.40, I63.9, I69.354). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2, female 1). Current outpatient medications are only metoprolol tartrate, carvedilol and famotidine (all valid through late 2026/2027); no anticoagulant is ordered and none appears anywhere in the record. Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention. Thrombocytopenia, non-ruptured cerebral aneurysm and a history of falling are documented and should be weighed in the risk/benefit discussion, but none is recorded as a decision to withhold therapy.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 2026-08-20 clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nonetheless re-ordered (valid 2026-08-20 to 2026-12-28) and remains current on 2026-09-24, together with aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg daily - triple antithrombotic therapy after a recent major GI bleed. interpretations.explanation: Irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 131 bpm (RR 0.36-0.62 s, RMSSD 143 ms) with no organised P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis +57 deg, no bundle branch block. QTc (Bazett) ~354 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (107819285, 11:18) was regular sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with clear P waves (PR 122 ms), so atrial fibrillation is new; QTc essentially unchanged (390 -> 354 ms).

QTc ~387 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (106516875, 2024-12-05) showed a 144 ms QRS with an rSR' pattern and a broad terminal R in V1 plus wide S waves in I/V6 - right bundle branch block - which has resolved on this tracing; QTc also fell from 470 to 387 ms (>60 ms decrease). Most likely a transient rate-related right bundle branch block.

The prior tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07) showed atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response (mean 47 bpm, RMSSD 189 ms) and QTc 419 ms. Regular rhythm at 69 bpm with a small consistent atrial deflection about 140 ms before each QRS - sinus rhythm (nursing documentation the same day records normal sinus rhythm). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block. The frontal axis is about -171 deg, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant: lead I and lead II are both deeply negative while aVR is positive, a pattern that in practice usually reflects left/right arm lead reversal and should prompt a repeat tracing with checked electrode placement. QTc (Bazett) ~378 ms. Only ECG for this patient.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR 122 ms, QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +44 deg. Repolarisation is clearly prolonged: QT ~490 ms with a Bazett QTc of about 530 ms. The prior tracing (107149156, 2020-06-17) was sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QTc ~374 ms, so QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. The patient remains on citalopram 40 mg daily (flagged separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +68 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~445 ms - below the 500 ms review threshold. Only ECG for this patient. This tracing was obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started and satisfies the post-initiation ECG requirement.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, PR 174 ms, QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis -9 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~357 ms. The prior tracing (108651109, 2018-12-13) was sinus at 66 bpm with a longer PR of 204 ms; nursing documentation that day noted intermittent atrial pacing. No rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change (391 -> 357 ms).

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm - RR intervals are 0.40-0.45 s with a coefficient of variation of only 0.02 and RMSSD 11 ms, i.e. regular, excluding atrial fibrillation - with low-amplitude atrial activity preceding each QRS (PR ~178 ms) and no sawtooth flutter waves on spectral analysis of the QRST-subtracted signal; this is best classified as sinus tachycardia. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +5 deg, QTc ~362 ms. The prior tracing (109839112, 2022-07-11) was atrial fibrillation (mean 110 bpm, coefficient of variation 0.24, RMSSD 190 ms, no P waves), so atrial fibrillation has resolved. Nursing notes on 2022-07-13 still record atrial fibrillation and atrial pacing, so the classification of this single tracing should be confirmed clinically.
Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, PR 164 ms, QRS 98 ms (upper normal, no bundle branch block), frontal axis +35 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~450 ms. Only ECG for this patient, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response: grossly irregular RR intervals (0.63-1.86 s, coefficient of variation 0.25, RMSSD 436 ms) at a mean of about 53 bpm, with no organised P waves and no measurable PR interval. QRS 106 ms - non-specific intraventricular conduction delay that does not meet criteria for right or left bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -33 deg (borderline left axis deviation). QTc ~412 ms. The prior tracing (100466541, 2024-09-04) was also atrial fibrillation (mean 81 bpm, QRS 108 ms, QTc 407 ms): no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular RR, coefficient of variation 0.21, RMSSD 172 ms, no organised P waves, no measurable PR interval) at a mean ventricular rate of about 99 bpm, with a very wide 158 ms QRS showing a QS complex in V1-V2 and a broad monophasic R in V5-V6 and lead I - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -16 deg. QTc ~429 ms. The tracing four days earlier (103262474, 2024-12-03) was regular sinus rhythm at 79 bpm with first-degree AV block (PR 240 ms) and a 146 ms QRS of right bundle branch block morphology (terminal broad R in V1 with wide S waves in I and V6) and marked left axis deviation. Therefore atrial fibrillation is new, the previous right bundle branch block has resolved and a new left bundle branch block has appeared; QTc change (474 -> 429 ms) is under 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular, PR 128 ms, QRS 78 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis -24 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~419 ms. The prior tracing (102616671, 2021-05-16) was sinus at 87 bpm with PR 142 ms and QTc 393 ms; no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 126 ms, QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +51 deg. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: QT ~485 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 518 ms. Compared with the prior ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23: sinus 75 bpm, QTc 361 ms) QTc has increased by more than 60 ms. This is the most recent tracing and the patient remains on escitalopram, so the prolongation is clinically actionable (flagged separately as a QT safety item).

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with first-degree AV block (PR 218 ms). QRS is widened to 126 ms with a deep QS pattern in V1-V2, a broad notched monophasic R in V6 and lead I and no septal q waves - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -24 deg. QTc (Bazett) ~476 ms (partly secondary to the conduction delay). The prior tracing (103686933, 2024-06-03) was essentially the same: sinus 68 bpm, PR 220 ms, QRS 124 ms with the same left bundle branch block, QTc ~465 ms. No new rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +47 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~430 ms. The prior day's tracing (101016166, 2025-03-18) is virtually identical (sinus 102 bpm, PR 134 ms, QTc 427 ms); no change.

Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular RR intervals (RMSSD 251 ms, 92% of successive intervals differing by >50 ms) at a mean ventricular rate of about 87 bpm, with no organised atrial activity, so no measurable PR interval. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR coefficient of variation 0.01), with a P wave before each QRS at PR 140 ms. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +69 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~406 ms. This is the only ECG for this patient, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 101 bpm with PR 150 ms, QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +62 deg and QTc ~421 ms. The immediately preceding tracing from the same day (102910502, 2021-08-23) is essentially identical (sinus 101 bpm, PR 154 ms, QTc 419 ms); no change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, with a low-amplitude but consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 170 ms). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +41 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~403 ms. 71-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 42731; carried in the history of every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease from coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). No anticoagulant has ever been prescribed - the only current outpatient order is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily (valid 2026-07-28 to 2027-01-01). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation (score >=2 in a man) is absent; note prior hemorrhage complicating a procedure should be weighed when selecting therapy.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0) and prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis (I63.40, I63.9, I69.354). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior stroke 2, female 1). Current outpatient medications are only metoprolol tartrate, carvedilol and famotidine (all valid through late 2026/2027); no anticoagulant is ordered and none appears anywhere in the record. Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention. Thrombocytopenia, non-ruptured cerebral aneurysm and a history of falling are documented and should be weighed in the risk/benefit discussion, but none is recorded as a decision to withhold therapy.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The required cardiology review of whether to resume anticoagulation is not documented.

Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no discernible P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Nursing rhythm documentation on 2026-06-10 also records atrial fibrillation. The charted rhythm and rate contradict the tracings and the patient (unspecified atrial fibrillation, on warfarin) needs rate/rhythm reassessment.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug per the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo) is current (order 2026-04-23, valid to 2027-01-02) and has been continued without interruption since 2024-05-14. The patient's most recent 12-lead ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT approximately 485 ms and Bazett QTc approximately 518 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which the clinic document requires the prescriber to review. Notably the 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this same tracing as "QT acceptable"; QTc had risen from 361 ms on the prior ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23). Most recent electrolytes are normal (K 4.1 mEq/L and Mg 2.1 mg/dL, both 2025-08-23). No ECG has been obtained since 2023.

Prescriber review is required by the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo. Most recent electrolytes (2026-04-20) are normal: K 4.4 mEq/L, Mg 2.2 mg/dL. Also on warfarin, which amiodarone potentiates.

The most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT approximately 490 ms and Bazett QTc approximately 530 ms (>=500 ms), compared with 374 ms on the prior tracing (107149156, 2020-06-17). Prescriber review is required by the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. Documented syncope and type 1 diabetes add to the concern; no ECG has been obtained since 2023.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) is current (order 2026-08-22, valid to 2027-01-05) and has been continuous since 2022-03-01. Additional risk: age 95, CKD stage 3, and concomitant warfarin/metoprolol. No ECG since 2022.

interpretations.explanation: Irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of about 131 bpm (RR 0.36-0.62 s, RMSSD 143 ms) with no organised P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis +57 deg, no bundle branch block. QTc (Bazett) ~354 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (107819285, 11:18) was regular sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with clear P waves (PR 122 ms), so atrial fibrillation is new; QTc essentially unchanged (390 -> 354 ms).

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular, with a P wave before each QRS (PR ~150 ms). QRS is now narrow at 82 ms; the frontal axis is rightward (net negative lead I, positive aVF, about +135 deg). QTc ~387 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (106516875, 2024-12-05) showed a 144 ms QRS with an rSR' pattern and a broad terminal R in V1 plus wide S waves in I/V6 - right bundle branch block - which has resolved on this tracing; QTc also fell from 470 to 387 ms (>60 ms decrease). Most likely a transient rate-related right bundle branch block.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with a small but consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 174 ms). QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +69 deg. Repolarisation is prolonged with a long isoelectric ST segment and a late broad T wave: QT ~515 ms, Bazett QTc ~522 ms. The prior tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07) showed atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response (mean 47 bpm, RMSSD 189 ms) and QTc 419 ms. Amiodarone was started 2025-11-10, so sinus rhythm has been restored (resolved atrial fibrillation) at the cost of a QTc rise of more than 60 ms to above 500 ms.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 111 bpm (RR coefficient of variation 0.01) with a small P wave identifiable before each QRS at PR ~128 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +60 deg, QTc ~409 ms. The prior day's tracing (106143775, 2025-03-07) was also a regular sinus tachycardia at 116 bpm with QTc 351 ms; the 58 ms QTc rise is below the 60 ms threshold, and there is no rhythm or conduction change.

Atrial fibrillation: markedly irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.28, RMSSD 249 ms) at a mean ventricular rate of about 99 bpm with no discernible P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -59 deg (left axis deviation, qR in I/aVL with deep S in II/III/aVF - left anterior fascicular block pattern). QTc ~421 ms. Only ECG available for this patient, so no prior comparison. Confirms the documented atrial fibrillation for which warfarin is prescribed.

Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, PR 136 ms, QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +42 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~444 ms. The prior tracing (100698634, 2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with PR 128 ms and QTc ~420 ms; rate has slowed but there is no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with a P wave before every QRS (PR 120 ms). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +39 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~457 ms (borderline prolonged but below the 500 ms review threshold). Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.33-0.55 s, RMSSD 98 ms) at a mean rate of about 144 bpm, with a fibrillatory baseline and no organised P waves, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +7 deg, QTc ~357 ms. The tracing two hours earlier the same day (107914094, 17:13) showed the same rhythm at 139 bpm with QTc 368 ms - no change. This directly contradicts the same-day clinic note describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' (flagged as a documentation conflict).

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, PR 154 ms, QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -28 deg (borderline leftward but within the normal range); lead II is nearly isoelectric. QTc (Bazett) ~443 ms. The prior tracing (104232242, 2025-04-27) was sinus at 60 bpm with QTc 405 ms; no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with a P wave before every QRS (PR 116 ms). QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis +6 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~425 ms (the T wave has a slow terminal limb, so the estimate carries roughly +/-30 ms uncertainty). Only ECG for this patient, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregular RR intervals (RMSSD 66 ms, 48% of successive intervals differing by >50 ms) at a mean of about 144 bpm, no organised P waves and therefore no measurable PR interval. Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, very regular, PR 152 ms, QRS 66 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +58 deg and QTc (Bazett) ~401 ms. Entirely normal tracing. Only ECG available, so no prior comparison.

The prior tracing (108234665, 2024-09-28) was sinus rhythm at 59 bpm with PR 156 ms and QTc ~378 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; QTc unchanged. Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm, PR 162 ms, QRS 94 ms (no bundle branch block), frontal axis +8 deg, QTc ~400 ms. Compared with the tracing two days earlier (102573205, 2026-02-17: sinus 83 bpm, PR 146 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 398 ms) there is no significant change - same rhythm, no new conduction abnormality and QTc within 2 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm. The P wave begins about 210 ms before the QRS, i.e. first-degree AV block (PR >200 ms). QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis +3 deg, QTc (Bazett) ~377 ms. The prior tracing (103042067, 2024-11-30) was sinus at 51 bpm with PR 184 ms and QTc 358 ms, so PR has lengthened slightly; rhythm unchanged, no new bundle branch block and QTc change well under 60 ms.

Two narrow, high-amplitude pacing spikes (slew several times greater than the QRS itself) precede each complex, about 110 ms and 80 ms before the R peak, followed by a wide 152 ms paced QRS with a markedly rightward frontal axis (about +131 deg; dominant negativity in I/aVL and tall R in III/aVF). No intrinsic P wave is visible, so no PR interval can be measured, and the intraventricular conduction pattern cannot be classified as right or left bundle branch block in a paced complex. QTc ~412 ms. The prior tracing (103417522, 2020-11-03) had no pacing spikes: a regular rhythm at 109 bpm with a very wide 192 ms QRS of left bundle branch block morphology (QS in V1-V2, broad monophasic R in V6) and QTc ~448 ms. Pacing is therefore new.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (coefficient of variation 0.19, RMSSD 104 ms) at a mean of about 152 bpm, no organised atrial activity and no measurable PR interval. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis -10 deg, QTc ~354 ms. The previous day's tracing (107374881, 2025-09-12) was sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with a clear P wave (PR 150 ms) and QTc 412 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; the QTc fall of 58 ms is just below the reporting threshold and is largely rate related. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response: irregularly irregular RR intervals (0.33-0.55 s, RMSSD 98 ms) at a mean rate of about 144 bpm, with a fibrillatory baseline and no organised P waves, so no measurable PR interval.
